en.name: Halibut
en.summary: Halibut is the giant of the flatfish, sold as thick white steaks and loins with dense, meaty flesh. From purchase it keeps 1–2 days in the fridge and 6–8 months in the freezer. It is lean, which is why it freezes so well and why it overcooks so easily.
en.pantry: Halibut must not be kept at room temperature. Its thickness gives it a little more grace than a thin flatfish fillet, but the surface is where spoilage starts and the surface warms first. Bring it home cold and follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour if it is above 32 °C (90 °F). Do not leave steaks out to come up to temperature before cooking; a cold steak cooks perfectly well, and halibut has no margin to waste.
en.fridge: Keep halibut at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on a rack over ice in a container that catches the melt water, and cook it within 1–2 days from purchase. Pat the steaks dry and store them in a single layer — not stacked, which traps moisture between them. Leave the skin on if it came with skin; it protects the flesh. Store it on the bottom shelf, below anything ready to eat. Halibut is very lean, so the flesh dries rather than going oily-stale as it ages.
en.freezer: Halibut keeps 6–8 months at −18 °C (0 °F), which is a long window for fish and a consequence of how little fat it carries. Freeze steaks individually, wrapped airtight with no air pockets, or ice-glazed by dipping in cold water and freezing the film that forms. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality. Because the flesh is so lean, freezer burn shows up quickly on a badly wrapped piece as white, dry, opaque patches.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight on a plate, or in a sealed bag under cold running water. Never on the counter or in warm water. Pat it dry, cook it promptly, and do not refreeze raw fish.
spoilage: A sour or ammoniacal smell rather than a clean, almost sweet one.
Flesh that stays dented when pressed instead of springing back.
A sticky or milky film on the cut surface, or liquid pooling underneath.
Gaping flesh where the flakes have separated, or a grey-yellow cast.
tips: Buy thick steaks or loin pieces; thin tail cuts dry out fast.
Store in a single layer on a rack over ice.
Wrap very carefully before freezing — lean flesh burns easily in the freezer.
Cook it just to opaque; halibut is unforgiving past that point.

faq.q: How long does halibut keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 days from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on ice and in a single layer.
Yes, 6–8 months at −18 °C. Wrap each steak airtight or ice-glaze it; lean flesh gets freezer burn quickly if it is exposed.

faq.q: What are the white dry patches on my frozen halibut?
faq.a: Freezer burn from air reaching the surface. It is not unsafe, but the texture is lost — trim the patches or use the piece in a soup.

faq.q: How can you tell if halibut has gone off?
faq.a: A sour or ammoniacal smell, a sticky film, flesh that will not spring back, or flakes that have started to gape apart.

zh.name: 大比目魚
zh.summary: 大比目魚是扁身魚裡的巨人，通常切成厚實的白肉魚排或背肉出售，肉質緻密。從購買日起冷藏可放 1～2 天，冷凍 6～8 個月。它非常低脂，這既是它耐凍的原因，也是它一煮過頭就柴的原因。
zh.pantry: 大比目魚不能放室溫。它夠厚，比薄魚片多一點寬容度，但腐敗是從表面開始的，而表面最先回溫。請保冷帶回家，並守 2 小時原則，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。不要為了「先回溫再煎」把魚排放在外面；冰的魚排一樣煎得很好，而大比目魚沒有可以浪費的餘裕。
zh.fridge: 架在網架上、下面鋪冰，容器要能接住融水，放 4 °C 以下，並在購買後 1～2 天內煮掉。魚排先擦乾、單層平放——不要疊起來，疊放會把水氣困在中間。帶皮的就留著皮，皮會保護魚肉。放最下層，位置低於所有即食食品。大比目魚極瘦，所以它變老的方式是「變乾」，而不是出現陳油味。
zh.freezer: 大比目魚在 −18 °C 下可放 6～8 個月，以魚類來說很長，原因就是它幾乎沒有脂肪。魚排請一片片分開包，密封不留空氣，或浸冷水做冰鍍。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質。也因為肉太瘦，包裝不確實的話很快就會出現凍燒——表面一塊塊乾白不透明的斑。
zh.thawing: 放盤子上冷藏隔夜解凍，或密封裝袋用冷水沖。不要放室溫或泡溫水。擦乾後盡快烹調，生魚不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有氨味，而不是乾淨帶甜的魚味。
按壓後凹陷回不來，而不是有彈性。
切面出現黏膜或乳白薄膜，或下方積水。
肌肉纖維整片裂開分離，或魚肉泛灰泛黃。
tips: 買厚魚排或背肉；薄的尾段很快就乾。
單層架在網架上、放冰的上方。
冷凍前包裝要非常確實——瘦肉很容易凍燒。
煎到剛好不透明就起鍋；過頭之後它不會原諒你。

faq.q: 大比目魚冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 鋪冰單層平放、4 °C 以下，從購買日起 1～2 天。
可以，−18 °C 下 6～8 個月。每片密封包好或做冰鍍；瘦肉一旦暴露很快就凍燒。

faq.q: 冷凍魚上那些乾白斑塊是什麼？
faq.a: 是空氣接觸造成的凍燒。不至於不安全，但質地已經壞了——切掉那些部位，或整片拿去煮湯。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷大比目魚不新鮮了？
faq.a: 發酸或氨味、表面黏膜、按壓沒有彈性，或肌肉纖維開始裂開。
